neighbours.label: Defining a quantitative measure as an explicit ratio of a numerator to a denominator.
fire: The average speed is calculated as the distance traveled divided by the elapsed time.
For this exercise, concentration is the amount of solute divided by the solution volume.
The worksheet defines productivity as the number of finished units divided by the hours worked.
Here the error rate equals the number of incorrect answers divided by the number attempted.
The manual defines efficiency as useful output energy divided by input energy.
To obtain the unit price, divide the total cost by the number of items purchased.
In this example, pressure is the force applied divided by the surface area.
The study defines participation rate as the count of attendees divided by the count invited.
quiet: A chart of average speed summarizes how quickly the vehicle traveled during the journey.
The exercise describes concentration as a way of comparing stronger and weaker solutions.
Our worksheet discusses productivity in a factory where workers make finished units.
The error rate indicates how often the students gave incorrect answers on the exercise.
A section of the manual discusses efficiency and ways to reduce wasted energy.
The unit price helps shoppers compare the cost of differently sized packages.
The example illustrates pressure using a force applied over a flat surface.
The participation rate helps the study team describe attendance among invited people.

notes: Ratio definitions separated in two exploratory pairs, whereas merely listing components did not. The opposite pole emphasizes extent or scope; this hypothesis concerns an explicit calculation of a measure. The card also contains unrelated price and technical-detail peaks, so coverage is uncertain.
